items.component: Calendar, DatePicker (Angular isDateDisabled; one violation order in the four adapters)
items.summary: Angular hw-calendar and hw-date-picker gain the isDateDisabled predicate that React, Vue and vanilla have, and hw-date-picker gains unavailableMessage. The four adapters ask one core helper which constraint a typed date violates, so the message chosen for a date that breaks two constraints is the same everywhere.

surface.angular: hw-calendar: `@Input() isDateDisabled?: (value: string) => boolean` (optional, no default). hw-date-picker: `@Input() isDateDisabled?: (value: string) => boolean` (optional) and `@Input() unavailableMessage = ''`, required under the text contract while isDateDisabled is given: `texts.need('unavailableMessage', unavailableMessage, 'isDateDisabled is given')`. Angular Forms error added by validate(): `{calendarUnavailable: {actual: string}}`.
surface.core: new export getDateViolation and type DateViolation

endState.dom: hw-calendar: a day the predicate rejects is a `button.hw-calendar-day` with the native `disabled` attribute, exactly as a day outside min/max (React calendar.tsx:68); it is never the roving tab stop. hw-date-picker: a typed date the predicate rejects gives violation 'unavailable': aria-invalid="true" on the text input, custom validity = unavailableMessage (a single space when the text is missing) and the message in the single p.hw-error of item dates-7.
endState.behaviour: Keyboard in the grid: an arrow, Home, End or Page key that lands on an unavailable day continues day by day in the direction of travel for at most 366 days and does not move when that leaves min/max; Angular keeps clamping the first target to min or max, as Vue does (vue/src/calendar.ts:207-208). Click, Enter and Space on an unavailable day change nothing and notify nothing. A typed ISO date that is unavailable still becomes the value (docs/date-input.md:13-15) and blocks submission. Violation order in every adapter: '' for an empty draft; 'invalid' when the draft is not an ISO date; 'unsupported' when the calendar cannot show it; 'invalid' when it is outside min/max; 'unavailable' when isDateDisabled returns true. Server rendering: the predicate runs during rendering on both sides and must be pure.

core.signature: type DateViolation = '' | 'invalid' | 'unsupported' | 'unavailable'; getDateViolation(draft: string, options: {min?: string; max?: string; calendar: CalendarSystem; isDateDisabled?: (value: string) => boolean}): DateViolation

Returns '' when draft is ''; 'invalid' when !isDateInRange(draft); 'unsupported' when !isCalendarDateSupported(draft, options.calendar); 'invalid' when !isDateInRange(draft, min, max); 'unavailable' when options.isDateDisabled?.(draft) is true; otherwise ''. No text, no Intl, no DOM.

items.summary: The message for a malformed, out-of-range, unsupported or unavailable typed date is one p.hw-error after the hint in the four adapters, with role=alert because the component produces it, and the vanilla controller renders it too. The Angular label gains the required marker, and aria-invalid follows the one rule of the conventions.

surface.react: none public. Internal: Field / FieldLayout prop `errorRole?: 'alert'` (react/src/shared.tsx:99), the flag of convention hint-error-validation-message; the rich-inputs-files specification assumes the same name.
surface.vue: none public. Internal: decorate(props, id, content, extraClass?, decorationId = id, produced?: VNodeChild) (vue/src/forms.ts:33).
surface.angular: hw-date-picker: `label` loses `{required: true}` (required only when the control has no aria-label, aria-labelledby or surrounding hw-field label); `describedBy` is replaced by the inherited `aria-describedby` input; `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-invalid` inherited from HwValueControl (forms-core).
surface.vanilla: New optional authored slot `[data-hw-error]` inside the root; no new option.

endState.dom: Order inside the field in every adapter: label.hw-label (with span.hw-required-marker when required), div.hw-date-picker-control, hint, error. One `p.hw-error#{controlId}-error`: with the application's `error` it holds that text and has no role; otherwise, while the draft violates a constraint and its message text exists, it holds the message with role="alert"; ISO dates inside a produced message are wrapped in `<bdi dir="ltr">`. No element when neither applies or the text is missing. Text input: aria-describedby = application ids, the id of output.hw-date-picker-value while it shows a date, field ids, hint id, error id (the four of the convention keep their order; the formatted value is read before hint and error); aria-invalid="true" exactly when error, an explicit aria-invalid, a failed submission or a violation applies. Vue's p#{id}-validation-error and Angular's p#{id}-date-error are gone. Vanilla: the message is written into an authored [data-hw-error] element when the root has one (role=alert set while it applies, authored text restored after), else into a created p.hw-error inserted after the root's .hw-hint, or as the last child of the root.
endState.behaviour: The message appears when a non-empty draft violates a constraint (on input) and disappears when the draft becomes valid or empty and on a form reset. The same text is the input's custom validity; a missing text gives a single space, no element and one development warning. A failed submission (the input's `invalid` event) sets aria-invalid until the input is valid again or the form resets; the event is not default-prevented. A required, empty, untouched picker has no aria-invalid. Server rendering: no p.hw-error is produced unless the application passes `error`; the `invalid` listener is attached after mount.

core.behaviour: The one source of the violation in the four adapters.

items.component: Calendar, DatePicker (native form reset)
items.summary: A native form reset returns Calendar and DatePicker to their reset target in the four adapters and notifies once when the value changed; in Angular, without Angular Forms, the picker no longer shows an empty field while it submits the edited date. Draft, visible month, dialog and submission aria-invalid return to their initial state in the same step.

Calendar: the selected day, the tab stop and the visible month are those of the reset target.
endState.behaviour: Reset target: React and Vue `defaultValue` (else ''); Angular the value held after the first ngOnInit unless Angular Forms is attached (then the component writes nothing itself and shows what Angular Forms wrote); vanilla the authored value (`input.defaultValue`, Calendar: options.value or data-hw-value). Calendar month target: defaultMonth (React), the `month` prop (Vue), the month input held after the first ngOnInit (Angular), options.month or data-hw-month (vanilla), else the month of the reset target. The calendar system is not reset. Read-only and disabled pickers are reset too. Timing and prevention are those of observeFormReset. The calendar inside the picker's dialog is not a form control of the surrounding form (form="" on its hidden input; vanilla: no reset observer); only the picker resets it.
